references.text: Consecrate to me every firstborn, whatever opens the womb among the Israelites, both of humans and animals; it belongs to me.
The commandment to give the firstborn to the Lord, including redemption money for firstborn sons.
You shall bring the first of all the fruit of your land to the house of the Lord your God.
Whatever opens the womb belongs to me, also every firstborn of your livestock, both oxen and sheep.
Rules concerning the firstborn and how they are to be redeemed or offered to the Lord.
Every male firstborn that is born in your livestock you shall consecrate to the Lord your God.
The firstfruits of all the fruit of the earth shall be brought to the sanctuary of the Lord.
Honor the Lord with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your produce.
Israel is my firstborn son - showing the significance of the firstborn for the Lord.
Numbers 18:15 expands on the law in Exodus 22:28 by specifying the principle of redemption money for human firstborns.
Deuteronomy 18:4 clarifies the giving of 'full grain and new wine' mentioned in Exodus 22:28 as part of the priest's rights.
Exodus 13:12 is a direct legal parallel confirming the duty to surrender every firstborn to the Lord.
It creates a theological contrast: Exodus 22:28 is the law about giving the firstborn to God, while 4:23 shows the consequence for one who refuses to let go of God's firstborn.
Exodus 34:20 explains the mechanism for 'giving' the firstborn son mentioned in Exodus 22:28 through redemption money.
Numbers 18:12 confirms the requirement to give the best parts of 'new wine' and grain mentioned in Exodus 22:28 to the priestly service.
